title: Human-AI Collaboration for Backend Text Generation: Dynamic Content Recommendation for Websites based on Keywords
abstract: A keyword-driven content recommendation engine that uses GPT-based pipelines to generate and personalize backend website copy.
question: How can GPT-based pipelines generate and personalize website copy from keywords, and how does it compare with human-written copy?
method: Co-developed the keyword-driven recommendation engine, then compared its output with human-written baselines in user studies with 40+ participants who scored coherence, relevance and preference.
findings: Reduced manual authoring time by 60%. The paper won Best Paper, 3rd Place at the 2024 International Conference on Computing and Data Science (ICCDS).

title: Sentiment-Based Drug Recommendation System
abstract: An NLP pipeline that classifies the sentiment of patient reviews and turns it into ranked drug recommendations.
question: Can the sentiment in patient reviews be used to rank drug recommendations?
method: Co-developed an NLP pipeline with a fine-tuned BERT model on domain-specific patient review data, and compared it against TF-IDF and LSTM baselines.
findings: Reached 88% classification accuracy, with a 12-point F1 improvement over the baselines from transfer learning with biomedical pretraining.

title: Automated Pneumonia Detection using DenseNet
abstract: A DenseNet-121 model that detects pneumonia in chest X-rays.
question: How well does DenseNet detect pneumonia in chest X-rays compared with other common CNNs?
method: Co-trained DenseNet-121 on the CheXpert chest X-ray dataset with augmentation and class weighting to handle label imbalance, and benchmarked it against ResNet-50 and VGG-16.
findings: Reached 92% precision-recall AUC on the held-out test set. DenseNet beat the other models by 6% AUC, thanks to dense skip connections that let layers reuse features.
